material_systems.name: Acrylic Latex Sealant

products: DAP Alex Plus Acrylic Latex Caulk Plus Silicone
sealant.notes: Standard acrylic latex for low-movement trim joints on painted wood. Paintable immediately after skinning (~30 min). 5-10 year lifespan. Movement class +-7.5% to +-12.5%. Lowest cost option — adequate for standard trim-to-siding and window perimeter joints where movement is minimal.

material_systems.notes: Best for low-movement joints: trim_to_siding, window_perimeter, corner_board. NOT suitable for expansion joints or joints with movement >+-12.5%.

material_systems.name: Siliconized Acrylic Sealant

products: DAP Alex Flex Premium Molding & Trim Sealant
sealant.notes: Improved water resistance over straight acrylic. Paintable immediately after skinning. 10-15 year lifespan. Still low movement class — not for expansion joints. Mid-range cost.

material_systems.notes: Step up from acrylic latex — better water resistance and flexibility. Same joint locations as acrylic but longer service life. Suitable for joints with moderate moisture exposure.

material_systems.name: Polyurethane Sealant

sealant.notes: High-performance polyurethane for expansion joints, concrete, and high-movement applications. SCHEDULING IMPACT: 3-7 day full cure required before ANY paint or primer can be applied over caulked joints. Lower yield per tube — typically serves wider joints. Class 25 or Class 50 movement capacity.

scheduling_gate.blocks: All finish coat tasks in adjacent painting specs
scheduling_gate.reason: Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling on uncured polyurethane. No exceptions.

material_systems.notes: Best for expansion joints, penetrations, and material transitions with movement >+-12.5%. Schedule caulking early — the 3-7 day cure gate delays finish coats on ALL adjacent painting specs.

material_systems.name: Hybrid MS Polymer Sealant

sealant.notes: Premium option — combines silicone-like durability with paintability. Paintable after skin forms (~1-2 hours). 20-30 year lifespan. Class 25 movement capacity. Highest cost among paintable sealants but best long-term performance and shorter paint wait than polyurethane.

material_systems.notes: Premium sealant for clients wanting maximum longevity without polyurethane scheduling impact. Suitable for all joint locations except high-movement expansion joints (>+-25%). No cure gate — paint after skinning.

SYS_EXT_CAULK_ACRYLIC.notes: Standard 1/4 inch bead on typical trim joint. Higher yield on narrow joints, lower on wider gaps.

SYS_EXT_CAULK_SILICONIZED.notes: Same yield as acrylic — similar bead profile and joint widths.

SYS_EXT_CAULK_POLYURETHANE.notes: Lower yield — polyurethane typically serves wider joints (3/8 inch+) with thicker bead. Expansion joints consume more material.

SYS_EXT_CAULK_HYBRID.notes: Similar yield to polyurethane — typically used in wider joints. Premium cost per LF.

joint_width_modifier.notes: Multiplier applied to base LF/tube yield. Wider joints consume proportionally more sealant per LF.

coverage_profiles.waste_notes: 10% material waste for caulking — accounts for gun waste (sealant left in tube nozzle/tip), partial tubes at end of run, and tooling waste. Lower than paint waste (15%) because application is more controlled.
assumptions: Base yield assumes 1/4 inch bead width on standard trim joint.
Backer rod joints use the same sealant yield per LF — backer rod controls depth, not sealant volume significantly.
10.1 oz standard cartridge for all systems.

consumables.name: Caulk Gun (smooth-rod professional)
consumables.notes: Smooth-rod preferred over ratchet for professional use — better bead control and smoother application. Reusable across projects. One per crew member applying sealant.

consumables.name: Closed-Cell Backer Rod
consumables.usage_rate: 1 LF backer rod per 1 LF joint
consumables.notes: Closed-cell foam backer rod. Multiple diameters available: 1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4, 1 inch. Select diameter = joint width x 1.25 for compression fit. Sold in 20-100 ft rolls. Required when joint width > 3/8 inch to prevent three-sided adhesion and control sealant depth (2:1 width:depth ratio). Conditional on joint_complexity = backer_rod.

consumables.name: Masking Tape for Clean Sealant Lines
consumables.notes: Painter's tape applied along both sides of joint for clean sealant line on visible/finished surfaces. UV-resistant exterior grade. Not all joints require tape — used on visible trim-to-siding and window perimeter joints against finished surfaces. Conditional on finished adjacent surfaces.

consumables.name: Utility Knife / 5-in-1 Tool
consumables.notes: For cutting caulk tube tips, trimming excess sealant, and light joint cleaning on NC joints. Reusable tool. 5-in-1 tool preferred — also serves as putty knife and scraper.

consumables.name: Drop Cloth (ground protection)
consumables.notes: Lightweight drop cloth below caulking work area to catch sealant drips and tube waste. Minimal coverage needed — caulking produces very little overspray. Canvas or plastic acceptable.

ext_ground_cover.description: Ground surface directly below caulking work area
ext_ground_cover.notes: Drop cloth at base of work area. Minimal coverage — caulking waste is limited to tube drips and cut-off bead trimmings. Protection quantity derived from joint LF footprint, not SF surface area.

ext_surface_adjacent.description: Adjacent finished surfaces requiring clean sealant lines
ext_surface_adjacent.notes: Tape both sides of joint on finished/visible surfaces. Uses 2x joint LF of tape (both sides). Not all joints require taping — estimator discretion based on surface finish state. No dedicated PaintScope key — quantity derived from joint LF.

compatibility_rules.description: Silicone sealant is NEVER permitted for paintable joints
compatibility_rules.notes: Silicone repels all paint. Paint will not adhere to silicone or silicone residue. If a joint requires painting, silicone must not be used. If silicone was previously applied, it must be completely removed — no solvent or primer can create adhesion over silicone. HARD STOP.

compatibility_rules.description: Polyurethane requires 3-7 day cure before painting
compatibility_rules.notes: Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling on uncured polyurethane. This is an absolute scheduling gate — no exceptions regardless of weather, urgency, or tier. Impacts ALL adjacent painting specs.

compatibility_rules.description: Acrylic latex limited to low-movement joints only
compatibility_rules.notes: Acrylic latex movement capacity is +-7.5% to +-12.5%. Using acrylic on high-movement joints (expansion, material transitions) will cause cohesive failure. Route high-movement joints to polyurethane or hybrid_ms.

compatibility_rules.description: Backer rod required when joint width exceeds 3/8 inch
compatibility_rules.notes: Joints wider than 3/8 inch without backer rod have improper width:depth ratio and risk three-sided adhesion — both cause premature failure. Auto-escalate joint_complexity to backer_rod. Backer rod diameter = joint width x 1.25.

compatibility_rules.description: Three-sided adhesion prohibited on all joints
compatibility_rules.notes: Sealant must bond only to two opposing sidewalls. Three-sided adhesion (sealant bonded to sidewalls AND joint bottom) restricts movement and causes premature cohesive failure. Backer rod (or bond-breaker tape for shallow joints) is mandatory whenever joint bottom would otherwise bond to sealant.

compatibility_rules.description: Caulk AFTER substrate primer, BEFORE finish coats
compatibility_rules.notes: Sealant adhesion is improved on primed surfaces. Finish coats must cover cured sealant to create continuous weatherproof envelope. Sequence: clean substrate → substrate primer → caulk → cure → finish coats. Per Exterior_Caulking_Sealants_Doctrine.md §3.

risk_notes.risk: Polyurethane requires 3-7 day full cure. Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling. Caulk beads (~40 mils) shrink as they cure — paint film (1-3 mils) cracks if applied too early.
risk_notes.mitigation: Enforce 3-7 day cure gate. Schedule caulking early in project. Alternative: use hybrid_ms or acrylic if schedule cannot accommodate polyurethane cure time.

risk_notes.risk: Any silicone residue on a joint surface prevents paint adhesion. Paint beads, peels, or fisheyes over silicone-contaminated surfaces.
risk_notes.mitigation: Never use silicone on paintable joints. If silicone was previously applied, complete removal is required — no primer or solvent can restore adhesion over silicone.

risk_notes.topic: Three-sided adhesion causing premature joint failure
risk_notes.risk: Sealant bonded to both sidewalls AND joint bottom cannot flex with joint movement. Cohesive failure (sealant tears internally) occurs within 1-3 years.
risk_notes.mitigation: Install backer rod as bond-breaker on joint bottom. For joints too shallow for backer rod, apply bond-breaker tape. Never fill joints solid with sealant.

risk_notes.risk: Acrylic latex has only +-7.5% to +-12.5% movement capacity. Expansion joints and material transitions can exceed this, causing adhesive or cohesive failure.
risk_notes.mitigation: Route high-movement joints (expansion, penetration at material transitions) to polyurethane (Class 25/50) or hybrid_ms (Class 25). Movement class routing table in research.json.

risk_notes.risk: Undersized backer rod falls into joint cavity — does not control depth or prevent three-sided adhesion. Oversized rod is difficult to install and may bow joint edges.
risk_notes.mitigation: Size backer rod at 1.25x joint width for proper compression fit. Closed-cell foam standard. Verify rod seats 1/4 inch below joint surface to allow proper sealant depth.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Sealant type selection is driven by expected joint movement: low-movement trim joints → acrylic_latex or siliconized_acrylic (lowest cost, no scheduling impact). Medium-movement joints → hybrid_ms (premium but short paint wait). High-movement expansion joints → polyurethane (best movement class but 3-7 day cure gate). Silicone is NEVER used on paintable joints.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Coverage varies primarily by joint width. Standard 1/4 inch bead yields ~30-35 LF/tube. Wider joints (3/8-1/2 inch) reduce yield to 20-25 LF/tube. Backer rod controls sealant depth but does not significantly change sealant volume per LF — the width is the primary variable.
material_notes.environmental_requirements: Most sealants require surface temperature above 40F and dry substrate. Polyurethane is moisture-cure — high humidity accelerates cure but low humidity slows it. Acrylic latex freezes below 32F during cure. No sealant should be applied to wet or frost-covered joints.
material_notes.no_quality_tier: This spec does NOT use quality_tier (QT2-QT5). Sealant type selection replaces quality tier as the cost/quality driver. Every caulk joint either meets the standard (proper adhesion, width:depth ratio, movement class) or it fails — there is no 'economy caulk' grade.

assumptions.value: 25-35 LF per 10.1 oz tube depending on sealant type and joint width
assumptions.note: Doctrine confirms 25-35 LF/tube range. Acrylic/siliconized at 30 LF baseline, polyurethane/hybrid at 25 LF baseline due to wider joints served.

No doctrine-specific waste factor for caulk. 10% is conservative — accounts for tube nozzle waste, partial tubes, and tooling waste. Lower than paint waste (15%) because application is more controlled and contained.

assumptions.value: 1 LF backer rod per 1 LF joint
assumptions.note: Backer rod is installed continuously in the joint — 1:1 linear relationship. Add 5% waste for cuts and compression fitting.

assumptions.value: Caulk joint LF captured via direct estimator input (IN_LF_CAULK_JOINT_TOTAL), not PaintScope key
assumptions.note: No dedicated PS_EXT key for caulk joint LF exists. Estimator captures joint LF directly during takeoff or derives from trim/opening LF keys. May warrant a PS_EXT key in v2.

uncertainty_flags.description: What percentage of caulk joints require tape masking for clean lines? Research says 'not all joints require tape' but does not quantify. Assumed 50% of joint LF on visible surfaces.
uncertainty_flags.action: Validate against field practice. May need estimator-level override for tape coverage percentage.

uncertainty_flags.description: Hybrid MS polymer sealants are less commonly stocked at paint suppliers than acrylic or polyurethane. Product availability may vary by region.
uncertainty_flags.action: Verify local availability before specifying hybrid_ms. May require special order with lead time.
